candidates.name: OpenAI Agents SDK JS/TS

webLite.evidence: The repository is TypeScript-first and the factory already depends on @openai/agents for Node-based provider calls.

wechatMiniGame.evidence: Use only in the local factory control plane; do not ship the SDK in a mini-game runtime.

douyinMiniGame.evidence: Use only in the local factory control plane; do not ship the SDK in a mini-game runtime.

tapTapMiniGame.evidence: Use only in the local factory control plane; do not ship the SDK in a mini-game runtime.

attributionDuties: Retain the MIT copyright and permission notice when distributing substantial copies.
approvedScope: tracing and handoff metadata in the factory control plane
candidates.rationale: It fills the packaging and observability gap without replacing the factory's Zod artifacts, state machine, pause/resume protocol, or workspace permission boundary.

candidates.name: LangGraph JS

webLite.evidence: Node/TypeScript compatible, but its graph runtime would duplicate the existing factory state machine.

wechatMiniGame.evidence: Not a mini-game runtime dependency; only a server/control-plane candidate.

douyinMiniGame.evidence: Not a mini-game runtime dependency; only a server/control-plane candidate.

tapTapMiniGame.evidence: Not a mini-game runtime dependency; only a server/control-plane candidate.

attributionDuties: Retain the MIT copyright and permission notice if adopted.
candidates.rationale: Checkpointers and interrupts are valuable, but adding a second durable graph would split ownership of the existing resumable state machine and increase migration risk.

candidates.name: Mastra

webLite.evidence: TypeScript workflows and human-in-the-loop are relevant to the control plane.

attributionDuties: Track Apache-2.0 notices for core code.
Do not import code from ee directories without reviewing the separate enterprise license.
candidates.rationale: The mixed license boundary and broad framework surface are unnecessary for the narrow packaging problem.

candidates.name: Microsoft AutoGen

webLite.evidence: The primary supported surface is Python/.NET and the repository README directs new projects to Microsoft Agent Framework.

attributionDuties: Retain the MIT copyright and permission notice if adopted.
candidates.rationale: Maintenance mode, cross-language integration cost, and an explicitly recommended successor make it a poor fit for this TypeScript factory.

conclusion.architectureDecision: Reuse the already-installed OpenAI Agents SDK only as a typed control-plane adapter around the existing Zod artifact contracts and resumable state machine. Introduce a local AgentPackage registry and prompt/context wrapper; keep generated game workspaces and all mini-game platform adapters independent of the SDK.
